title: Incarnatus est
readingOutcome: Parse perfect passive constructions and participial agreement.

authoringPolicy.method: short concept introduction → authentic example → guided recognition → controlled manipulation → liturgical reading → retrieval
authoringPolicy.vocabularyPolicy: Only the frozen Lesson 16 allocation is introduced; later clause vocabulary is explicit support.
authoringPolicy.authenticTextPolicy: Perfect passive is anchored in the Credo and scriptural clauses used in the Roman liturgy.
authoringPolicy.copyrightPolicy: Pedagogical prose and exercises are original synthesis.

sources.sourceLatin: Et incarnatus est de Spiritu Sancto ex Maria Virgine: et homo factus est.
sources.provenanceNote: incarnatus est is the principal perfect-passive construction; factus est is recycled as a parallel.

sources.sourceLatin: Crucifixus etiam pro nobis: sub Pontio Pilato passus, et sepultus est.
sources.provenanceNote: Crucifixus/passus/sepultus provide coordinated participial predicates with passive/perfect meaning.

sources.sourceLatin: Qui traditus est propter delicta nostra, et resurrexit propter justificationem nostram.
sources.provenanceNote: traditus est gives perfect passive trado beside active perfect resurrexit.

sources.sourceLatin: Multi enim sunt vocati, pauci vero electi.
sources.provenanceNote: electi gives a plural perfect-passive participle and agreement anchor.

sources.sourceLatin: Et hoc vobis signum: invenietis infantem pannis involutum, et positum in praesepio.
sources.provenanceNote: signum is introduced in a Nativity clause; participles are reading support, not silently taught grammar beyond the lesson target.

casePanel.policy: All six cases remain active. Participles are read through the same agreement system as adjectives.

perfectPassiveFramework.construction: perfect passive participle + present of sum
perfectPassiveFramework.agreement: The participle agrees with the grammatical subject in gender, number and case.
perfectPassiveFramework.deponentPreview: nascor and morior form perfects with participles + sum but have active meaning; the general deponent system is deferred to Lesson 19.

learningBlocks.title: A participle plus sum can make a completed passive

learnerCopy.en: Latin often forms the perfect passive with a perfect passive participle plus a present form of sum: incarnatus est, crucifixus est, sepultus est. Read the participle as an agreeing adjective that also carries verbal meaning.
learnerCopy.fr: Le latin forme souvent le parfait passif avec un participe parfait passif et une forme présente de sum : incarnatus est, crucifixus est, sepultus est. Lisez le participe comme un adjectif accordé qui porte aussi un sens verbal.

learningBlocks.title: The participle agrees with its subject

learnerCopy.en: incarnatus and crucifixus are masculine singular because their understood subject is Christ. electi is masculine plural because it refers to the 'few' who are chosen. Agreement is therefore part of parsing the verb construction.
learnerCopy.fr: incarnatus et crucifixus sont masculins singuliers parce que leur sujet sous-entendu est le Christ. electi est masculin pluriel parce qu'il se rapporte aux « peu nombreux » qui sont choisis. L'accord fait donc partie de l'analyse verbale.

learnerCopy.en: incarnatus est is completed passive meaning. In the same sentence, factus est gives a second participle + sum construction already partly familiar from earlier reading.
learnerCopy.fr: incarnatus est exprime un accompli passif. Dans la même phrase, factus est fournit une seconde construction participe + sum, déjà partiellement familière.

learnerCopy.en: The Creed compresses three actions. Crucifixus and sepultus are passive in meaning; passus belongs to the deponent patior and has active meaning 'suffered'. This contrast prepares Lesson 19 without teaching the whole deponent system early.
learnerCopy.fr: Le Credo condense trois actions. Crucifixus et sepultus ont un sens passif ; passus appartient au déponent patior et signifie activement « souffrit ». Ce contraste prépare la leçon 19 sans anticiper tout le système des déponents.

learnerCopy.en: traditus est is perfect passive: he was handed over. resurrexit is perfect active: he rose again. The two completed actions have different voices, and the morphology tells you which.
learnerCopy.fr: traditus est est un parfait passif : il fut livré. resurrexit est un parfait actif : il ressuscita. Les deux actions sont accomplies, mais leur voix diffère.

learningBlocks.title: Do not confuse participle shape with voice meaning

learnerCopy.en: nascor, morior and patior remind you that some verbs have passive-looking forms but active meaning. For now, recognize these named exceptions; Lesson 19 will generalize the deponent system.
learnerCopy.fr: nascor, morior et patior rappellent que certains verbes ont des formes d'apparence passive mais un sens actif. Pour l'instant, reconnaissez ces exceptions nommées ; la leçon 19 généralisera le système.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Et incarnatus est de Spiritu Sancto ex Maria Virgine: et homo factus est.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Et incarnatus est de Spiritu Sancto ex Maria Virgine: et homo factus est.

translation.en: And He became incarnate by the Holy Ghost of the Virgin Mary: and was made man.
translation.fr: Et il s'est incarné du Saint-Esprit dans le sein de la Vierge Marie, et il s'est fait homme.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Crucifixus etiam pro nobis: sub Pontio Pilato passus, et sepultus est.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Crucifixus etiam pro nobis: sub Pontio Pilato passus, et sepultus est.

translation.en: He was crucified also for us: suffered under Pontius Pilate, and was buried.
translation.fr: Il fut aussi crucifié pour nous ; sous Ponce Pilate il souffrit et fut enseveli.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Qui traditus est propter delicta nostra, et resurrexit propter justificationem nostram.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Qui traditus est propter delicta nostra, et resurrexit propter justificationem nostram.

translation.en: Who was delivered up for our sins, and rose again for our justification.
translation.fr: Lui qui fut livré pour nos fautes et ressuscita pour notre justification.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Multi enim sunt vocati, pauci vero electi.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Multi enim sunt vocati, pauci vero electi.

translation.en: For many are called, but few are chosen.
translation.fr: Car beaucoup sont appelés, mais peu sont élus.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Et hoc vobis signum: invenietis infantem pannis involutum, et positum in praesepio.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Et hoc vobis signum: invenietis infantem pannis involutum, et positum in praesepio.

translation.en: And this shall be a sign unto you: you shall find the infant wrapped in swaddling clothes and laid in a manger.
translation.fr: Et voici le signe qui vous est donné : vous trouverez un enfant enveloppé de langes et couché dans une mangeoire.
